Chapter 10: The Meaning of Contingency
You know, there’s a certain comfort in thinking the world just makes sense—that everything happens for a reason, and that things are exactly as they’re meant to be.
But when we look at the story told by the Burgess Shale, we see something very different—a world shaped not by destiny, but by chance and pure happenstance.
Picture this: in the ancient Cambrian seas, a sudden storm hits, the tides shift, or maybe a new predator shows up out of nowhere.
Each of these moments has the power to change everything.
Down there, survival isn’t always about being the toughest or the smartest.
Sometimes, it’s just about being in the right place at the right time—about luck.
For scientists who study the Burgess Shale, this idea is both a little bit humbling and oddly freeing.
It tells us that the world we know is just one outcome among countless possibilities, brought to life by a long string of accidents and lucky turns.
If things had gone a little differently, the creatures ruling the planet today might look nothing like us, or anything we recognize.
And yeah, that sense of contingency, of everything hinging on chance, can be unsettling.
It pushes back against the idea that humans—or any creature—were somehow destined to appear.
Instead, it reminds us that our own existence comes from a long, unpredictable chain of events, filled with surprises and missed opportunities.
The Burgess Shale, with all its forgotten creatures and lost worlds, is a powerful signal that history is never set in stone—and the future? It’s always wide open.
And if you’re willing to lean into that uncertainty, there’s actually a sense of freedom in it.
The world isn’t rigid or predetermined. It’s open, dynamic—constantly being shaped.
The story of life is still being written, and you—you get to be part of it.
